newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Babcock unit expects to break even in 97.
newsitem.headline: D.Babcock unit expects to break even in 97.

text.p: BDAG Balcke-Duerr AG, a unit of troubled German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG, said on Friday it expected to break even in 1996/97 after sales and orders rose in the first half of the year.
The firm said the high level of orders and improvements from restructuring measures should lead to a second half that offsets a 35 million mark ($20.6 million) loss in the six months to March 31.
"From today's view the board is going on the basis of a break-even result for the current year," said Balcke-Duerr, an engineering company invovled building a new airport in Athens.

In the first half of 1996/97, sales rose 24 percent to 794 milion marks while orders rose 36 percent to 1.27 billion marks. Overseas orders increased more than 150 percent and made up 56 percent of the total.
Profit was hurt by restructuring expenses, operating costs related to old contracts based on low prices and further costs to expand international business, the company said.
Balcke-Duerr expected a net profit in the following business year, based on the high level of orders and improved price levels.

Deutsche Babcock, which owns 67 percent of Balcke-Duerr, nearly collapsed last summer and has tried to refocus on core businesses after sustaining a 400 million mark pretax loss in the year that ended September 30, 1996.
